threats.title: Unauthenticated Access
threats.description: An attacker reaches a protected function without presenting valid credentials.

threats.title: Credential Exposure
threats.description: Stored credentials are recovered in plaintext or a reversible form after a data store compromise.

threats.title: Offline Password Cracking
threats.description: A stolen password hash is cracked offline because it used a weak or unsalted hashing scheme.

threats.title: Brute Force Login
threats.description: An attacker submits a large number of password guesses against the login endpoint.

threats.title: Credential Stuffing
threats.description: An attacker replays credentials leaked from other breaches against the login endpoint.

threats.title: Account Takeover
threats.description: An attacker gains persistent control of a privileged account using a single compromised factor.

threats.title: Token Replay
threats.description: A password reset or similar single-use token is reused or replayed after its intended window.

threats.title: Session Hijack
threats.description: An attacker continues to use a session that should have been invalidated after a security-relevant event.

threats.title: Client-side Authorization Bypass
threats.description: An attacker calls a protected API directly, bypassing authorization checks that only exist in client-side UI code.

threats.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference
threats.description: An attacker accesses another user's object by manipulating an identifier, without an accompanying ownership check.

threats.title: Privilege Escalation
threats.description: A low-privilege identity gains access to functionality or data reserved for a higher-privilege role.

threats.title: Mass Assignment
threats.description: An attacker sets a privileged field (e.g. role, isAdmin) by including it in a request body the server binds without filtering.

threats.title: SQL Injection
threats.description: External input changes the structure of a SQL query executed by the application.

threats.title: Cross-Site Scripting
threats.description: An attacker injects script into a page viewed by other users because user-controlled content is rendered without proper output encoding.

threats.title: Unrestricted File Upload
threats.description: An attacker uploads a file of an unexpected type or size that is later executed, served, or used to exhaust storage.

threats.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
threats.description: An attacker causes the server to make an outbound request to an internal or unintended destination on the attacker's behalf.

threats.title: NoSQL Injection
threats.description: External input changes the structure or semantics of a query executed against a non-relational data store.

threats.title: Insecure Deserialization
threats.description: Untrusted serialized data is deserialized into objects without validation, allowing an attacker to influence application state or achieve code execution.

threats.title: Excess Network Exposure
threats.description: A service or management interface is reachable from the public internet when it does not need to be, widening the attack surface.

threats.title: Overprivileged Cloud IAM Role
threats.description: A workload or user identity holds broader cloud permissions than its function requires, increasing the impact of any single compromise.

threats.title: Unpatched Known-Vulnerable Dependency
threats.description: A component runs a version with a publicly known vulnerability because it was not updated within a reasonable window.

threats.title: Lateral Movement via Flat Network
threats.description: An attacker who compromises one host uses an unsegmented network to reach other hosts, including data stores, directly.

threats.title: Unrecoverable Data Loss
threats.description: Backups do not exist, are not encrypted, or cannot be restored, so a destructive incident causes permanent data loss.

threats.title: Insufficient Security Logging
threats.description: A security-relevant event occurs without producing a log record, preventing detection or investigation after the fact.

threats.title: Log Tampering or Deletion
threats.description: An attacker with access to a compromised host modifies or deletes local logs to cover their tracks.

threats.title: Untested Incident Response Plan
threats.description: An incident response runbook exists on paper but has never been exercised, so it fails or is too slow when a real incident occurs.

threats.title: Unaudited Privileged Action
threats.description: A privileged identity performs a sensitive action with no record of who did it or when, preventing accountability and forensic review.
